questions.q: In this lab's scenario, what duplicated block appears identically in the Onboarding, Offboarding, and Equipment Request flows?
options: Notify the employee's manager, wait for a decision, and log that decision and its date onto the triggering record
Creating a new employee record from scratch
Sending a weekly scheduled report to HR
Deleting the triggering record after approval
questions.explain: All three flows independently build the same notify-manager, wait-for-decision, log-decision sequence — the exact duplication Lesson 13 warned about.

questions.q: Per Step 1 of the lab, what confirms the duplicated block is actually safe to extract into a subflow?
options: The flows are owned by the same administrator
The steps are identical in order across all three flows, and the only differences are data (which record, which message) rather than different logic
All three flows were built in the same week
The flows all use the If/Else action somewhere
questions.explain: Identical steps with only data-level differences (the kind of thing a parameter can carry) is the signal that extraction is safe — different underlying logic would not be.

questions.q: What Inputs does the lab design for the new 'Notify and Log Manager Decision' subflow?
options: Manager, Request Record, and Message
Only a single generic Record input
Decision and Decision Date
Employee Name and Department only
questions.explain: Manager (who to notify), Request Record (what the decision applies to), and Message (the wording, which varies by caller) are exactly what each of the three flows needs to supply.

questions.q: After building the subflow, what does Step 4 have each of the three calling flows do?
options: Keep their original inline logic unchanged, in addition to calling the subflow
Delete the duplicated inline block and replace it with a single Call Subflow action, mapping that flow's own data pills into the subflow's inputs
Rebuild the subflow's logic a second time inside each flow for safety
Remove the Request Record input entirely from each flow
questions.explain: Extraction means the logic now lives in exactly one place; each calling flow is reduced to one Call Subflow action with its own pills mapped into that subflow's inputs.

questions.q: What does Step 5's verification expect to confirm after the refactor?
options: That all three flows now behave differently than before, since the logic moved
That the subflow produces a different decision than the original inline logic did
That all three flows behave exactly as they did before the change — same notification, same logged decision, same date — because only where the logic lives changed, not what it does
That the Request Record input can be removed since it's no longer needed
questions.explain: A refactor changes where logic lives, not what it does — verifying unchanged behavior is exactly how you confirm the extraction didn't introduce a regression.
